cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to tell you about a normalization operation that is probably the most ubiquitous, so the most widely used
cues.zh: 講師：這部影片要介紹一種正規化運算，可能是整個統計領域最普遍、也就是使用最廣泛，

cues.en: and probably the most important transformation in all of statistics, therefore, all of applied statistics in machine learning,
cues.zh: 而且可能最重要的轉換，因此在機器學習中的應用統計、

cues.en: in data analysis, in deep learning and so on.
cues.zh: 資料分析、深度學習等等領域，也都非常重要。

cues.en: It's called the Z-score.
cues.zh: 它叫做 Z 分數。

cues.en: Or if you are, you know, depending on which side of the Atlantic you're on, you might call this the Z-score, but whatever.
cues.zh: 或者，取決於你在大西洋的哪一側，也可能把 Z 唸成另一種發音，不過無所謂。

cues.en: And I've actually already introduced the idea of Z-score normalization in at least one video might've come up more often than that.
cues.zh: 其實我已經在至少一部影片中介紹過 Z 分數正規化的概念，也可能提過不只一次。

cues.en: Anyway, let's start with a problem statement.
cues.zh: 總之，先從問題開始。

cues.en: So imagine that we want to compare my height to someone else's weight.
cues.zh: 假設我們想把我的身高，和另一個人的體重相比。

cues.en: So your weight.
cues.zh: 也就是你的體重。

cues.en: Well, the problem which we can already imagine, I'm gonna show you a graph here, but we can already imagine what the problem is.
cues.zh: 問題其實已經可以想像得到，雖然等一下會展示圖形，但現在應該就能想到問題。

cues.en: The units are completely different.
cues.zh: 單位完全不同。

cues.en: Height is measured in, you know, inches or centimeters or whatever unit you want, and weight is measured in pounds or kilograms or stone or you know, whatever.
cues.zh: 身高可以用英吋、公分，或任何你想用的單位衡量；體重則用磅、公斤、英石等等。

cues.en: But these are not comparable, directly comparable metrics.
cues.zh: 但這些量值無法直接比較。

cues.en: So it might look something like this.
cues.zh: 圖形可能會像這樣。

cues.en: Here we have a graph of height in centimeters and weights in kilograms.
cues.zh: 這裡是以公分表示的身高，以及以公斤表示的體重。

cues.en: So let's say this is my height over here and this is your weight over here.
cues.zh: 假設這裡是我的身高，這裡是你的體重。

cues.en: How can we possibly compare this number to this number?
cues.zh: 要怎麼比較這個數字和那個數字呢？

cues.en: It just doesn't even make any sense.
cues.zh: 這根本沒有道理。

cues.en: It's apples and oranges.
cues.zh: 就像拿蘋果和橘子相比。

cues.en: So this is a problem statement.
cues.zh: 這就是問題。

cues.en: We need to come up with a way of being able to compare values across different scales.
cues.zh: 我們需要找出一種方法，能夠比較不同尺度上的數值。

cues.en: And the key insight here, the way that we are going to approach solving this problem is that maybe we don't need to care about my height in centimeters per se.
cues.zh: 解決這個問題的關鍵洞見是，也許我們不必在意我的身高以公分表示時，究竟是多少。

cues.en: Instead, what we can do is think about how my height compares to a sample or a population of other people's heights.
cues.zh: 反而可以想想，我的身高相對於其他人身高的樣本或母體，處在什麼位置。

cues.en: So let's say we go around, we take a survey, we measure a bunch of people, or we just, you know, look up online and we measure, I don't know how many, this is maybe a couple hundred people
cues.zh: 假設我們到處做調查，測量一群人的身高，或者上網查資料。不知道測了多少，這裡也許是幾百人，

cues.en: and we get all of their heights and it's distributed somewhere like this.
cues.zh: 取得所有人的身高，分布大致像這樣。

cues.en: And then we can see, here's my height here.
cues.zh: 然後可以看到，我的身高在這裡。

cues.en: So relative to this sample, wherever the, you know, whatever population this is drawn from, my height is roughly average, maybe a tiny little bit higher than average.
cues.zh: 相對於這個樣本，不管它來自哪個母體，我的身高大致接近平均，也許比平均高一點點。

cues.en: Okay and then we look at your weight.
cues.zh: 好，接著看你的體重。

cues.en: Again, we don't really care about your weight per se, but we take a group of people should be ideally the same population.
cues.zh: 同樣地，不太在意體重數字本身，而是找一群人，理想上應該是同一個母體。

cues.en: But anyway, we take a group of people and a couple hundred people and we look at their distribution of weights and then we see that your weight is around, you know,
cues.zh: 總之，找幾百人，看看他們的體重分布，再看到你的體重大約在這裡，

cues.en: maybe this is one standard deviation below the mean.
cues.zh: 也許比平均值低一個標準差。

cues.en: So that is the key idea of Z normalization.
cues.zh: 這就是 Z 正規化的關鍵概念。

cues.en: We don't care about the values per se.
cues.zh: 我們不在意數值本身。

cues.en: Instead, we are going to normalize or transform the data into some number that is a relative number relative to a certain distribution.
cues.zh: 而是要把資料正規化或轉換成相對數值，也就是相對於某個分布的數值。

cues.en: So now it is feasible to compare my height, which is a little bit above average, and your height, which is around, let's say it's one standard deviation below average weight.
cues.zh: 現在就能比較略高於平均的我的身高，和你的身高……也就是假設比平均體重低一個標準差的體重。

cues.en: Okay so that's the key insight and that is our solution.
cues.zh: 這就是關鍵洞見，也是解決方法。

cues.en: We want to normalize both measurements to a unitless scale.
cues.zh: 我們要把這兩種量測值，都正規化到沒有單位的尺度。

cues.en: And the key insight is that a value on its own is difficult to interpret.
cues.zh: 關鍵是，單獨一個數值很難解讀。

cues.en: So we don't actually care about anyone's height in centimeters.
cues.zh: 我們其實不在意任何人的身高究竟是幾公分。

cues.en: We don't actually care about any one person's weight in kilograms.
cues.zh: 也不在意某個人的體重究竟是幾公斤。

cues.en: What we care about is each value relative to a distribution.
cues.zh: 在意的是，每個值相對於分布的位置。

cues.en: And that is the insight.
cues.zh: 這就是關鍵洞見。

cues.en: That's why we need this Z normalization.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼需要 Z 正規化。

cues.en: Okay, so here's the formula for these Z-transform.
cues.zh: 好，這就是 Z 轉換的公式。

cues.en: It's really easy. You do first, you mean center the data.
cues.zh: 非常簡單，首先將資料平均中心化。

cues.en: So you subtract the average from each individual value.
cues.zh: 也就是從每個個別數值減去平均值。

cues.en: That's what you see here.
cues.zh: 這裡顯示的就是這個步驟。

cues.en: So the Z value for the ith element in the dataset is that dataset or that data element I, minus the average over all the data.
cues.zh: 資料集中第 i 個元素的 Z 值，等於這組資料，或者說第 i 個資料元素，減去所有資料的平均值。

cues.en: And then we call, and then we do what's called variance normalization, which is just dividing by the standard deviation.
cues.zh: 然後進行所謂的變異數正規化，也就是除以標準差。

cues.en: Maybe I should have called this standard deviation normalization, but I don't know.
cues.zh: 也許應該把它叫做標準差正規化，但我也不知道。

cues.en: Variance, V is a nicer letter than S maybe.
cues.zh: 也許是因為變異數的 V 比 S 好看。

cues.en: Okay, I have no excuse.
cues.zh: 好，我沒有藉口。

cues.en: It's a little confusing.
cues.zh: 這有點讓人困惑。

cues.en: But some people use variance in standard deviation interchangeably, which probably technically isn't really correct.
cues.zh: 不過有些人會把變異數和標準差混用，嚴格來說，這應該不太正確。

cues.en: But anyway, so what does that mean?
cues.zh: 總之，這是什麼意思？

cues.en: So we subtract the mean of the distribution and we divide by the standard deviation of that distribution.
cues.zh: 就是減去分布的平均值，再除以該分布的標準差。

cues.en: And that means that the units of Z are no longer in the original units.
cues.zh: 這表示 Z 的單位，不再是原本的單位。

cues.en: We have no more original units.
cues.zh: 原來的單位消失了。

cues.en: Instead we have units of standard deviations from the mean, from the center of the distribution.
cues.zh: 取而代之的是，距離平均值，也就是分布中心，有多少個標準差。

cues.en: And you can see just by looking at this equation that the units are gonna be gone because the numerator has units of centimeters or whatever's units, and the denominator also has the units
cues.zh: 只要看這個方程式就知道，單位會消掉，因為分子有公分或其他單位，而分母也有

cues.en: of centimeters.
cues.zh: 公分這個單位。

cues.en: So we're dividing centimeter by centimeter.
cues.zh: 所以是公分除以公分。

cues.en: That gives us a unitless measure.
cues.zh: 得到的就是沒有單位的量值。

cues.en: So again, the Z-transform is very simple.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，Z 轉換非常簡單。

cues.en: All you do is subtract the mean from each individual data point and divide by the standard deviation and the resulting units here for Z, the interpretation
cues.zh: 只要從每個個別資料點減去平均值，再除以標準差，而這裡得到的 Z 值，其解讀方式

cues.en: of the Z-transform data is that they are in standard deviation units.
cues.zh: 就是：Z 轉換後的資料，以標準差為單位。

cues.en: So going back to this example here, so I said, you know, I don't know if this is exact,
cues.zh: 回到這個例子，我不知道這是否完全精確，

cues.en: but let's say that you, your weight 52, 53 kilograms has a Z value of minus 1.
cues.zh: 但假設你的體重是 52、53 公斤，對應的 Z 值是 −1。

cues.en: That means that it is exactly one standard deviation below the mean.
cues.zh: 這表示恰好比平均值低一個標準差。

cues.en: Okay, so a couple of important points about the Z-transform.
cues.zh: 好，關於 Z 轉換，有幾個重要重點。

cues.en: The Z-transform shifts and stretches the data, but it doesn't change the shape of the distribution.
cues.zh: Z 轉換會平移並伸縮資料，但不會改變分布的形狀。

cues.en: So here you see the same histogram of heights in centimeters.
cues.zh: 這裡是同一組以公分表示的身高直方圖。

cues.en: Here I normalize them to Z values, and now they are heights in standard deviation units.
cues.zh: 這裡將它們正規化為 Z 值，現在身高是以標準差為單位。

cues.en: But you can see that the overall shape of the distribution is the same.
cues.zh: 但你可以看到，分布的整體形狀相同。

cues.en: It looks actually like a couple of the bars have different heights, but that's just because the number of bins actually changed here.
cues.zh: 看起來有幾個長條的高度不同，但這只是因為這裡的區間數其實改變了。

cues.en: So the exact bin width is not the same here and here.
cues.zh: 因此，這邊和這邊的實際區間寬度不同。

cues.en: That's why it looks like there are subtle differences.
cues.zh: 這就是看起來有細微差異的原因。

cues.en: In fact, we can plot one by the other.
cues.zh: 其實也可以將一個對另一個畫出來。

cues.en: So this is height in centimeters, this is height in Z-score.
cues.zh: 這裡是公分表示的身高，這裡是 Z 分數表示的身高。

cues.en: And you can see that they're perfectly correlated, perfectly linearly correlated.
cues.zh: 可以看到，它們完全相關，而且是完全線性相關。

cues.en: The correlation coefficient is 1.0.
cues.zh: 相關係數為 1.0。

cues.en: So we're not changing the distribution of the data.
cues.zh: 所以我們沒有改變資料的分布。

cues.en: All we're doing is shifting it on the X axis and then stretching it this way.
cues.zh: 只是沿著 X 軸平移，再往這個方向伸縮。

cues.en: And then the final thing I want to touch on here is the assumption underlying the Z-transform.
cues.zh: 最後想稍微談一下 Z 轉換背後的假設。

cues.en: So the question is what are the assumptions underlying this Z normalization procedure?
cues.zh: 問題是，這個 Z 正規化程序背後，有哪些假設？

cues.en: If you'd like to pause the video and give it some thought, then now is your opportunity to do so.
cues.zh: 如果想暫停影片思考一下，現在就是機會。

cues.en: So the assumptions under, okay, so, what is the key assumption that makes the Z-transform valid or appropriate for any given dataset?
cues.zh: 好，讓 Z 轉換對某組資料有效或適用的關鍵假設是什麼？

cues.en: The answer is that the mean and standard deviation, which are part of this formula are valid and useful descriptions of the distributions, central tendency and dispersion.
cues.zh: 答案是，公式中的平均值和標準差，能有效且有用地描述這個分布的集中趨勢與離散程度。

cues.en: That is basically just another way of saying that the distribution is roughly Gaussian.
cues.zh: 這基本上是換個方式說，分布大致呈高斯形狀。

cues.en: Again, I've said this many times before, but the distributions don't need to be perfectly Gaussian for the Z-transform to be appropriate.
cues.zh: 我之前說過很多次，分布不必是完美的高斯分布，Z 轉換才會適用。

cues.en: That's something you often see in statistical analyses in general, that many statistical analyses are robust to minor violations of their assumptions
cues.zh: 在統計分析中常會看到這件事，許多統計分析可以容忍輕微違反假設的情況，

cues.en: as long as those violations aren't so bad.
cues.zh: 只要違反程度不是太嚴重。

cues.en: Okay, so the data should be roughly gian distributed, roughly normally distributed, which means that the mean, the average value and the standard deviation are appropriate measures
cues.zh: 因此，資料應該大致呈高斯分布、大致呈常態分布，也就是平均值

cues.en: of central tendency and dispersion.
cues.zh: 與標準差，是適當的集中趨勢與離散程度量值。

cues.en: So if you have a data set that is distributed like this, then you know you can still, technically, you can still compute these Z-transform, you can still Z-normalize these data,
cues.zh: 如果資料集的分布像這樣，技術上仍然可以計算 Z 轉換，仍然可以對這些資料進行 Z 正規化，

cues.en: but it's going to be harder to interpret because they're gonna be in standard deviation units.
cues.zh: 但會比較難解讀，因為它們會以標準差為單位。

cues.en: And the standard deviation is not a very useful measure of dispersion, nor is the average value a really good measure of the central tendency
cues.zh: 而標準差並不是很有用的離散程度量值，平均值也不是很好的集中趨勢量值，

cues.en: of the clustering in the data.
cues.zh: 無法很好地描述資料聚集的位置。

cues.en: So does that mean you should never apply the Z-transform to data that are non-Gaussian distributed?
cues.zh: 這是否表示，絕對不能對非高斯分布的資料進行 Z 轉換？

cues.en: I don't know. It depends a bit on the specific application, but it is certainly the case that if you are applying the Z-transformation to data that are strongly non normally distributed,
cues.zh: 我不知道，要看具體應用。但可以確定的是，如果對嚴重偏離常態分布的資料套用 Z 轉換，

cues.en: then you have to make sure that you are interpreting the results really carefully.
cues.zh: 就必須非常謹慎地解讀結果。

cues.en: Okay, so in this video I covered Z-normalization or Z-score normalization.
cues.zh: 好，這部影片介紹了 Z 正規化，也就是 Z 分數正規化。

cues.en: It's important to understand to know the formula for Z-score normalization.
cues.zh: 理解並知道 Z 分數正規化的公式很重要。

cues.en: It's a pretty straightforward formula, so I think it's worth committing to memory.
cues.zh: 公式相當直接，所以我認為值得記下來。

cues.en: And it's also important to keep in mind the assumption underlying the Z-score normalization.
cues.zh: 也必須記住 Z 分數正規化背後的假設。
